root_cause.text: In the i915 GEM shmem scatterlist population (shmem_sg_alloc_table), adding folio pages to a scatterlist without capping the cumulative byte length against `max_segment` allowed the `unsigned int .length` field to overflow when the total length reached or exceeded 4 GB for a single scatterlist entry.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "When a scatterlists table of a GEM shmem object of size 4 GB or more is populated with pages allocated from a folio, unsigned int .length attribute of a scatterlist may get overflowed if total byte length of pages allocated to that single scatterlist happens to reach or cross the 4GB limit." The patch adds `max_segment / PAGE_SIZE` to the `nr_pages` calculation and ensures that when extending an existing scatterlist, `nr_pages` is limited by `(max_segment - sg->length) / PAGE_SIZE`. The comment `/* XXX: could overflow? */` in the original code confirms the risk was previously acknowledged but unaddressed.

The folio conversion changed the behaviour of shmem_sg_all
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:

Author: Matthew Wilcox (Oracle) <willy@infradead.org>
Date:   Tue Sep 19 20:48:55 2023 +0100

    i915: Limit the length of an sg list to the requested length
    
    The folio conversion changed the behaviour of shmem_sg_alloc_table() to
    put the entire length of the last folio into the sg list, even if the sg
    list should have been shorter.  gen8_ggtt_insert_entries() relied on the
    list being the right length and would overrun the end
bic_trace_step.reason: The diff shows the introduced fix: nr_pages = min_t(unsigned long, folio_nr_pages(folio), page_count - i) caps the number of pages added per scatterlist entry to the remaining needed pages, and this capped value is used for length (nr_pages * PAGE_SIZE) instead of the full folio_size. This addresses the root cause by preventing addition of more pages than the requested length, thus avoiding potential overflow of the sg->length field and overrun of the scatterlist.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shmem_get_pages function contains the vulnerable scatterlist accumulation logic. At lines 388-400, pages are added to a scatterlist entry with `sg->length += PAGE_SIZE` when `sg->length >= max_segment` is false. The check `sg->length >= max_segment` does not prevent overflow of the unsigned int `sg->length` if `max_segment` is large (e.g., near 4 GiB), because it compares the current length against the segment limit rather than ensuring the addition will not exceed the limit or overflow. This matches the root cause: cumulative byte length is not properly capped against `max_segment`, allowing `sg->length` to overflow when total length reaches 4 GiB. The fix that would prevent overflow (e.g., checking `sg->length + PAGE_SIZE > max_segment`) is not present.
